data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the test is installed as a precondition for the subject's existence in the registry, so that the subject cannot be said to exist independently of the test. Under these conditions the test is a constructive definition, not a descriptive instrument. The 3-of-26 result is a property of the installation ritual itself: the shown-to-fail-first installation makes the test's failure signature part of the subject's identity, so mutations that break that identity are constrained, while mutations that merely change the subject's behaviour without breaking the ritual are described.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The registry is a descriptive index, not a constructive one, so the test does not define the subject's identity","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 3-of-26 result is caused by the compiler's own import structure, not by the identity-constituting role of the installation ritual","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A test constrains its subject only when it is a necessary condition for the subject's intended function, not merely for registry membership","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'constructive identity': when acceptance into the registry requires a specific failure to be shown first, the test becomes a constitutive rule for the subject's identity in that registry. The subject is not 'a module that does X' but 'a module that passes this specific shown-to-fail guard'. The 3-of-26 distribution reflects the proportion of mutations that alter the subject's identity-constituting properties versus those that alter accidental properties.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
